note: Written for Verity's tests (not from any corpus). Each example: subject, body, optional html, sender. The legitimate list ends with everyday support requests (refunds, pricing, invoices) that the corpus alone mistook for spam; they are never used for training. The spam list likewise ends with spam that imitates support mail (phishing, fake invoices and delivery fees, cold pitches). Neither is in the training data, but they were used to choose the weight of scripts/support_*.txt, so they guard regressions rather than estimate accuracy. "uncertain" holds a message the base model scores between the two thresholds, for the possible-spam path.
